subject.title: v2026.6.x system prompt bloat causes instruction following degradation on smaller models

question: What prompt/context policy should OpenClaw adopt for smaller or stricter models: extend opt-in lean mode, add model-aware defaults, change skill activation priority, sequence the related bootstrap/tool/skill trackers, or define a new unified context-budget contract?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the permanent fix changes default prompt composition and may add or alter config, skill, tool, and bootstrap behavior that affects existing users and overlapping open PRs.

options.title: Coordinate a prompt-policy design
options.body: Keep this issue open as the regression tracker, use the related issues for bootstrap/tool/skill slices, and require smaller-model proof before changing defaults.

options.title: Land narrow mitigations only
options.body: Accept incremental fixes such as broader lean filtering or bootstrap tiering while explicitly leaving instruction-priority and skill-content conflicts tracked here.

options.title: Defer to existing knobs
options.body: Decline new core behavior and document localModelLean, tools allow/deny, contextInjection, and bootstrap caps as the supported workaround path.

recommendation.title: Coordinate a prompt-policy design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the regression tracker, use the related issues for bootstrap/tool/skill slices, and require smaller-model proof before changing defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest observed history across the prompt, bootstrap, and prior review surfaces that need a product/default decision.
